note: The week on the Special Intensive Revision in a few sentences, written every Friday from the What's new entries of the seven days to that Friday. Each sentence links to the page that carries the fact, with that page's name as the label. Every figure in a sentence is a figure in one of the week's entries, and sources lists the entries each issue draws on.

paragraphs.text: The Commission wrote on 6 November to the Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland that electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can be included in the final roll by submitting the enumeration form with a statement, and that a form accepted keeps the elector's earlier EPIC number.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: Uttar Pradesh's summary-revision draft roll is now due on 17 November, with claims and objections taken until 16 December and the final roll due on 4 January 2027.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: Karnataka's State Election Commission asked the Supreme Court on 12 November to let it hold the five Bengaluru corporation elections on the final rolls of 18 April 2026 and to complete them by 31 January 2027.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: The Calcutta High Court issued notice on 12 November on a petition over an Economically Weaker Section certificate withheld because a parent was deleted from the roll, and LiveLaw reported on 13 November that the court had agreed to hear an Army aspirant refused a domicile certificate because his mother was deleted.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: The Wire found that 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 West Bengal electors whom judicial officers found eligible and the Commission has appealed against have Muslim names by its classification, and the Hindustan Times reported from a report by the Civic Research Group that in 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts every elector found eligible faces an appeal against inclusion.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: In Delhi 32,35,212 of the electors sent the 33.1 lakh notices had been parked for the final roll by 4 November, and Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer put the electors found ineligible after a notice at 54,418 on 6 November.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: The registration officer of Delhi's Mustafabad sought an FIR against a booth level agent after officials found 36 of the 37 Form 7 applications naming the agent as objector to be false, and in Bhiwandi East in Maharashtra over 450 of 540 Form 7 applications were rejected because the electors were found living at their addresses.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: People Against SIR has called for peaceful protests across the country from 26 November to 20 December, beginning with demonstrations on Constitution Day.
paragraphs.label: Events

paragraphs.text: On 3 November the Election Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer that an elector left off the draft roll may file Form 6, and that no registration officer is to start action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 only because the elector was on an earlier roll and filed Form 6.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: The Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 in the states where the revision is still running and put it on ECINet as a separate form, The Indian Express reports.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: On 4 November the Commission ordered a special summary revision of the roll in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim, with the final rolls due on 21 January 2027, and West Bengal's special summary revision, put back on 28 October, now has its draft roll due on 23 November.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: On 4 November the Supreme Court said electors left off Delhi's draft need not fear filing Form 6 while it hears the case, declined urgent orders and will hear the petitioners' application on 19 November.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: On 4 November the Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre and the Commission on petitions against section 16 of the Act of 2023 on the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners, which bars civil and criminal proceedings against any of them, serving or former, and listed the petitions for 18 December.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: On 5 November the Bombay High Court at Goa held that a voter who moves house files Form 8 and cannot be made to file Form 6, directed the registration officer of Santa Cruz to include a family of six in the roll within ten days and refused the Commission a stay.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer gave 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases and 14,04,033 no-mapping cases on 4 November, with 14,88,802 and 7,95,415 of them still pending.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: Every state and union territory with a schedule for the revision now has a What to do now page, 32 in all, with the steps open to an elector on the day it is read, and a card on the front page leads to each of them.
paragraphs.label: Left off the roll? What to do

paragraphs.text: On 29 October the Election Commission moved the final rolls to 30 November in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Nagaland and to 22 December in Delhi, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officers.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: In an affidavit of 26 October the Election Commission told the Supreme Court that all three SIR orders were unanimous and that Form 6 was not amended, while accepting that the declaration shown online with it could be read as an amendment, and on 27 October the Court gave the petitioners 10 days to answer it.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: At the Delhi hearing of 28 October the Supreme Court said orally that electors left off the draft who were on the 2026 roll should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which is for first-time voters, and told the Commission to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 with no 30 October cut-off, and no written order was reported.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: On 30 October the Supreme Court told the Commission to examine the bulk Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that the petitioners say remain unresolved and to file a compliance report, and it declined to extend the time for Kerala's revision.
paragraphs.label: Protests and disputes

paragraphs.text: Meghalaya's final roll of 26 October holds 21,83,963 electors, a fall in the roll of 1,65,682 since the roll before the revision, and Karnataka's final roll of 27 October holds 4,54,55,689 general electors, a fall in the roll of 99,76,625 since the roll of 16 June.
paragraphs.label: Reserved seats, final rolls and borders

paragraphs.text: Telangana had held 92,08,443 hearings on notices by 29 October and found 50,690 electors ineligible, and Delhi had disposed of 31.2 lakh of its 33.1 lakh notices by 26 October.
paragraphs.label: How the revision was run

paragraphs.text: On the help page and on every state's page a box now shows whether claims and objections are open in that state today and when the final roll is due, and How the revision was run now lists the bulk Form 7 filings reported in each state.
paragraphs.label: Left off the roll? What to do

paragraphs.text: The INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner was put back to 31 October because of rain, and BJP marches run in Rajasthan from 30 October to 5 November and in six Uttar Pradesh regions from 3 to 5 November.
paragraphs.label: Events
